lines.trans: Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?

words.gram: m sg construct noun with b- (in)

lines.trans: Washed twice, Chef! I brought two baskets of ripe red berries and sweet almonds.
How are we going to solve the smudged blue ink at the bottom, Salma?
Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
Tin Two gets a tart lemon icing to balance the sweet ripe berries, yes?

words.gloss: for; because of; in order to

lines.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.

words.gram: f sg construct noun with w- (and)

lines.trans: Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!

words.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

lines.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?

lines.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.text: بتحبي قهوة ولا شاي أحمر؟
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: على شنتتي في شريطة حمرا.
examples.trans: There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.text: في حدا أخد شنتتي بالغلط!
examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!

examples.text: المباني القديمة بتاخد وقت لتسخن.
examples.trans: Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.text: الباص بيوصل بعد أربعين دقيقة.
examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.

examples.text: ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.text: لون سيارتي أزرق.
examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Form IV verb; in casual Jordanian speech often replaced by عاد, though نعيد is widely heard.

examples.text: إذا خربت الوصفة لازم نعيد الخبز من الأول.
examples.trans: If the recipe goes wrong we have to redo the baking from scratch.

examples.text: المعلم أعاد السؤال مرتين عشان الكل يفهم.
examples.trans: The teacher repeated the question twice so everyone would understand.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.text: أنا من الأردن.
examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: أنا وإياك رح نخلص المشروع قبل يوم الخميس.
examples.trans: You and I will finish the project before Thursday.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.text: أهلا، أنا طارق!
examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!

examples.text: أهلا فيكي ببيت الياسمين!
examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.text: أهلا فيكي بأول يوم شغل!
examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!

examples.text: اقرأ الصفحة الأولى بهدوء.
examples.trans: Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: أي سيارة بتفضل؟
examples.trans: Which car do you prefer?

examples.text: بأي ساعة رح يبلش الاجتماع اليوم؟
examples.trans: At what hour is the meeting going to start today?

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?

examples.text: ما صار ولا إشي، روق.
examples.trans: Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.text: إلى اللقاء يا أستاذ!
examples.trans: See you soon, sir!

examples.text: مع السلامة وإلى اللقاء.
examples.trans: Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.text: إنتي أكيد نور!
examples.trans: You must be Nour!

examples.text: إنتي بطلة اليوم يا نور.
examples.trans: You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.text: غسل إيديه بالمي الدافية.
examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.

examples.text: زرعت الورد بإيدي.
examples.trans: I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.text: اخترت هادي الحارة لسبب عائلي.
examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.

examples.text: اختاروا طاولة تحت الشجرة.
examples.trans: They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form X استنتج; denotes reasoning from clues.

examples.text: هاد استنتاج ذكي كتير من الأدلة الموجودة.
examples.trans: That is a very clever deduction from the available clues.

examples.text: وصلنا لاستنتاج واضح بعد ما قرأنا الكرت.
examples.trans: We reached a clear conclusion after reading the card.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.text: شو اسمك الكريم؟
examples.trans: What is your kind name?

examples.text: اسمي مكتوب هون عالدفتر.
examples.trans: My name is written here in the notebook.

اضطر.gloss: to have to; be forced to

meanings.en: to have to; be forced to
meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb ('have to do something').

examples.text: ما رح يضطر حدا يضيق عيونه عشان يقرأ اللوحة.
examples.trans: Nobody will have to squint to read the sign.

examples.text: اضطرينا ندهن الشيش جوا الممر بسبب المطر.
examples.trans: We had to paint the shutters inside the hallway because of the rain.

meanings.note: First working day of the Jordanian week (pronounced il-ahad).

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنرتب جدول الأسبوع كله.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we plan the schedule for the whole week.

examples.text: المدارس والمكاتب بعمان بتفتح يوم الأحد.
examples.trans: Schools and offices in Amman open on Sunday.

meanings.note: Commonly refers to mulberries, which are popular in Jordan, or any berry.

examples.text: عصير التوت كثير زاكي بالصيف.
examples.trans: Mulberry juice is very delicious in the summer.

examples.text: شجرة التوت بالحديقة صارت مليانة حبات سودة حلوة.
examples.trans: The mulberry tree in the garden is full of sweet dark berries now.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.text: بالزبط! صرتي منا وفينا.
examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.

examples.text: احكيلي بالزبط شو أشتري.
examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: بس نص كاسة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.text: اشرحلي الموضوع بكلام بسيط.
examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.

examples.text: المشكلة بسيطة وحلها سهل.
examples.trans: The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.text: بيوصل بعد أربعين دقيقة.
examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.

examples.text: يا سلام عالشمس بعد المطر!
examples.trans: How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: السيارة تبع أخوي خربانة.
examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.

examples.text: وين المفتاح تبع خزانة المطبخ؟
examples.trans: Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.text: القطة متخبية تحت الطاولة.
examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form II شطّب; used for interior finishing and culinary final touches.

examples.text: دهنة العسل هي أحلى تشطيب للكيكة.
examples.trans: A honey glaze is the nicest finish for the cake.

examples.text: خلصوا تشطيب الشقة قبل نهاية الشهر.
examples.trans: They finished the apartment's finishing work before month's end.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.text: عد للعشرة، واحد تنين تلاتة.
examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.text: بدي بس حبتين، تنين بيكفوا.
examples.trans: I only want two pieces, two are enough.

examples.text: جبنا كتابين تنين من رف الإعارة.
examples.trans: We brought two books from the lending shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb meaning to bring something. Can also mean 'you (m) brought'.

examples.text: جبت لك هدية معي.
examples.trans: I brought a gift with me for you.

examples.text: جبت معي مرطبان عسل وزبدة بلدية.
examples.trans: I brought a jar of honey and local butter with me.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of جد (grandfather); plural جدات.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يخبزوا بعسل وزبدة بلدية.
examples.trans: Our grandmothers used to bake with honey and local butter.

examples.text: رح نزور جدتي يوم الجمعة بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: We will visit my grandmother on Friday after lunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.text: أنا نور، موظفة الاستقبال الجديدة.
examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.

examples.text: ركبت لمبة جديدة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I installed a new lightbulb last week.

جنّن.gloss: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful

meanings.en: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful
meanings.note: Form II geminate verb. In Levantine speech, بيجنن ('it drives one crazy') is one of the warmest compliments for food, music, or places.

examples.text: ريحة المعجنات من الصبح بتجنن!
examples.trans: The smell of pastries from the morning is amazing!

examples.text: العزف اليوم جنن كل اللي قاعدين.
examples.trans: Today's playing amazed everyone sitting there.

meanings.note: Describes citrus, yogurt, or tart flavours.

examples.text: كريمة الليمون طلعت حامضة زيادة عن اللزوم.
examples.trans: The lemon icing turned out too sour.

examples.text: التوت الأخضر بعده حامض قبل ما يستوي.
examples.trans: Green berries are still tart before they ripen.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.text: القلم خلص حبره.
examples.trans: The pen ran out of ink.

examples.text: الحبر الأزرق نشف بسرعة عالورق السميك.
examples.trans: The blue ink dried quickly on the thick paper.

meanings.note: Geminate Form I verb; used for solving problems and untying knots.

examples.text: كيف رح نحل مشكلة الحبر الملطخ عالكرت؟
examples.trans: How are we going to solve the smudged ink problem on the card?

examples.text: طارق حل العقدة بسرعة بإيده.
examples.trans: Tariq untied the knot quickly with his hand.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.text: الفستان هذا كثير حلو عليك.
examples.trans: This dress is very beautiful on you.

examples.text: طعم العسل مع قشر البرتقال حلو ومتوازن.
examples.trans: The taste of honey with orange peel is sweet and balanced.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.text: قهوة مع حليب وسكر خفيف.
examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.

examples.text: فطور خفيف وزاكي الصبح.
examples.trans: A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.text: الجو اليوم كثير دافي.
examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Colloquial adjective describing honey, syrup, or gluey surfaces.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق بس طعمه بجنن.
examples.trans: Warm honey looks sticky, but its taste is amazing.

examples.text: إيديه صاروا دبقين من القطر.
examples.trans: His hands got sticky from the sugar syrup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.text: برجع بعد عشر دقايق بالزبط.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.

examples.text: استنى دقيقة واحدة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Noun of instance from دهن (to spread/brush).

examples.text: الكيكة بدها دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: The cake needs a light brush of warm honey.

examples.text: الحيط محتاج دهنة بوية جديدة قبل العيد.
examples.trans: The wall needs a fresh coat of paint before the holiday.

meanings.note: Hollow Form I verb (often pronounced داق in casual Jordanian).

examples.text: مين رح يذوق التلات كيكات ويختار الأحسن؟
examples.trans: Who is going to taste the three cakes and pick the best one?

examples.text: ذقت العسل البلدي وكان طعمه روعة.
examples.trans: I tasted the local honey and its flavour was wonderful.

meanings.note: Used in the warm Jordanian thank-you كلك ذوق ('you are all kindness / how gracious of you').

examples.text: كلك ذوق يا أستاذ، شكرا!
examples.trans: How kind of you, sir, thank you!

examples.text: ذوقك بالألوان هادي وجميل.
examples.trans: Your taste in colours is calm and lovely.

meanings.note: Active participle of ربح (to win).

examples.text: الورقة الرابحة تبعت سلمى كانت دهنة العسل.
examples.trans: Salma's winning card was the honey glaze.

examples.text: الفريق الرابح رح يحتفل بالساحة اليوم.
examples.trans: The winning team will celebrate in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Form III verb meaning 'keep a close eye on an oven, timer, or process'.

examples.text: أبو طارق بيراقب درجة حرارة الفرن والمؤقت.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq watches the oven temperature and the timer.

examples.text: أنا براقب من الكرسي وبعطيكم التعليمات.
examples.trans: I'll watch from the chair and give you instructions.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: رح أسافر بكرة.
examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.text: رفع الصندوق الثقيل لحاله.
examples.trans: He lifted the heavy box by himself.

examples.text: مازن رفع الصينية بحذر من جوا الفرن.
examples.trans: Mazen carefully lifted the tray out of the oven.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.text: شو رقم تلفونك؟
examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.text: بستناك من ساعة.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بسامح / سامح). سامحني / سامحوا means 'forgive me / excuse me'.

examples.text: سامحوا صوتي التعبان من السفر الطويل.
examples.trans: Forgive my tired voice from the long trip.

examples.text: سامحني يا معلم، ما كان قصدي.
examples.trans: Forgive me, boss, I did not mean to.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.text: بحب الشاي الأحمر بدون سكر.
examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.

examples.text: رشينا سكر ناعم فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.text: حطيت الليمون الأصفر بالسلة.
examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.

examples.text: رمى الورقة بسلة المهملات.
examples.trans: He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Common adjective describing boldness or bravery; plural is broken شجعان.

examples.text: طارق ولد شجاع ما بخاف من العتمة.
examples.trans: Tariq is a brave boy who is not afraid of the dark.

examples.text: هاي خطوة شجاعة كتير من فريق المطبخ.
examples.trans: That is a very courageous step from the kitchen team.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.text: كل شي جاهز عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.

examples.text: كلامك صح تماما.
examples.trans: What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صعبة, plural: صعبين).

examples.text: الخلافات العائلية دايما صعبة.
examples.trans: Family disagreements are always hard.

examples.text: الزبدة المالحة صعبة مع المربى الحلو.
examples.trans: Salted butter is tricky with sweet jam.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Used for a method of doing something, or sometimes a physical path.

examples.text: كل واحد إله طريقة في الشغل.
examples.trans: Everyone has their own way of working.

examples.text: هاي أسهل طريقة عشان توازن طعم الليمون.
examples.trans: This is the easiest way to balance the lemon flavour.

meanings.note: Used for giving directions (straight ahead) or referring to time (immediately).

examples.text: امشي طوالي وبعدين لف يمين.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead then turn right.

examples.text: روح طوالي لآخر الممر وبتلاقي المكتبة.
examples.trans: Go straight ahead to the end of the corridor and you will find the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.text: تفضلي شاي بالنعنع مع عسل.
examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.

examples.text: العسل الجبلي طعمه رائع.
examples.trans: Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.text: رحت عالدكتور عشان أنا مريض.
examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.text: الكتاب على الطاولة.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.text: البناية عمرها تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.

examples.text: طول عمره ساكن بهاد الحي.
examples.trans: He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!

examples.text: شو نعمل هلا والمطر نازل؟
examples.trans: What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.text: غسلت الفناجين وحطيتهم عالرف.
examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.

examples.text: اغسل إيديك قبل الأكل.
examples.trans: Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.text: هادي مش غلطتكم أبدا.
examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.

examples.text: صلحنا الغلطة بدقيقتين.
examples.trans: We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: Invariable culinary loanword treated grammatically as feminine in Jordanian recipes.

examples.text: حطي معلقة فانيليا صغيرة على خليط الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a small spoonful of vanilla into the cake batter.

examples.text: ريحة الفانيليا طالعة من المطبخ للدور التاني.
examples.trans: The scent of vanilla is drifting from the kitchen to the second floor.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of فائز with glide -y- replacing medial hamza; also serves as a predicate adjective.

examples.text: الفايز بالمسابقة رح ياخد علبة شوكولاتة.
examples.trans: The winner of the contest will get a box of chocolates.

examples.text: هنينا الفايزين بنهاية يوم التذوق.
examples.trans: We congratulated the winners at the end of tasting day.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.text: في ناس كثير بالسوق.
examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: لازم أوصل قبل الساعة خمسة.
examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.text: الساحة فيها شجرة ياسمين قديمة.
examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.

examples.text: دكان الخردوات القديم ورا الجسر.
examples.trans: The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.text: الجو كان بارد امبارح.
examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Colloquial noun from كشّر (to frown/scowl); describes a sour or grumpy facial expression.

examples.text: تغيرت كشرة وجهه لضحكة أول ما ذاق العسل.
examples.trans: The frown on his face turned into a smile as soon as he tasted the honey.

examples.text: بلاش هالكشرة الصبح، اليوم رح يكون حلو.
examples.trans: Drop that morning frown; today is going to be good.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.text: كل الناس بتحب الصيف.
examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective derived from European classic; used for traditional recipes, architecture, and music.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة الكلاسيكية ما بتتغير من زمان.
examples.trans: This classic recipe has not changed for ages.

examples.text: عزفوا مقطوعة كلاسيكية عالبيانو باللوبي.
examples.trans: They played a classical piece on the piano in the lobby.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.text: كيف حالك اليوم؟
examples.trans: How are you today?

examples.text: كيف قدرت تفتح القفل القديم بدون ما تكسره؟
examples.trans: How did you manage to open the old lock without breaking it?

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: عملت كيكة شوكولاتة لزاكية.
examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing 'sleeve' (kumm, pl. kmaam كمام) from كم ('how many?').

examples.text: شمرت عن كمامي قبل ما نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: I rolled up my sleeves before we washed the windows.

examples.text: تبللت كمام قميصي لما ركضنا تحت المطر.
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves got soaked when we ran in the rain.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.text: الشنتة الزرقا إلي.
examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: شكرا كتير إلكم!
examples.trans: Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.text: احكيلي كل شي لازم أعرفه.
examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.

examples.text: لازم كل شي يكون تمام!
examples.trans: Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Intransitive/transitive verb meaning 'stick fast' (paint on dry wood, stamp on postcard).

examples.text: الدهان ما بيلزق منيح عالخشب المبلول.
examples.trans: Paint does not stick well to wet wood.

examples.text: لزقنا ورقة المواعيد على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck the schedule sheet onto the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.text: إلى اللقاء، رحلتك سعيدة!
examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: الوضع لوز، لا تقلق.
examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الدافية جاهزة.
examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.

examples.text: عصرت نص ليمونة عالشوربة.
examples.trans: I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.text: ما أكلت إشي من الصبح.
examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبينة, plural: مبينين).

examples.text: القطار الخشب مبين قديم وغالي.
examples.trans: The wooden train looks old and precious.

examples.text: مبين إنه رح تمطر الليلة.
examples.trans: It looks like it is going to rain tonight.

meanings.note: Plural of متدرّب (trainee/apprentice), from تدرّب (to train).

examples.text: في متدرّب جديد عم بتعلم شغل الحلويات مع سلمى.
examples.trans: There's a new apprentice learning pastry work with Salma.

examples.text: المتدرّبين بالشركة ساعدوا بتجهيز المعرض.
examples.trans: The trainees at the company helped set up the exhibition.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متوترة, plural: متوترين).

examples.text: صوته عالتليفون كان متوتر شوي.
examples.trans: His voice on the phone sounded a little nervous.

examples.text: شاي النعنع بيهدي الأعصاب المتوترة.
examples.trans: Mint tea calms tense nerves.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from مثال (example, model); describes ideal timing, conditions, or results.

examples.text: حرارة الجو اليوم مثالية للجلسة بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The weather today is ideal for sitting in the garden.

examples.text: هادا المكان مثالي لتخبية صندوق الكنز.
examples.trans: This spot is ideal for hiding the treasure box.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from محل (place); refers to local products, markets, or customs.

examples.text: دايما بنشتري الزبدة والعسل من الإنتاج المحلي.
examples.trans: We always buy butter and honey from local production.

examples.text: الجريدة المحلية كتبت عن مهرجان الخبز.
examples.trans: The local newspaper wrote about the bread festival.

meanings.note: Passive-participle/place noun from Form VIII اختبر; denotes a science lab, culinary test room, or clinic lab.

examples.text: سلمى حولت المطبخ لمختبر تذوق صغير.
examples.trans: Salma turned the kitchen into a small tasting lab.

examples.text: الطلاب عملوا تجربة جديدة بمختبر الكيمياء.
examples.trans: The students ran a new experiment in the chemistry lab.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.text: رحت على البترا مرة وحدة.
examples.trans: I went to Petra one time.

examples.text: جربنا الوصفة مرة تانية بس بخففنا السكر شوي.
examples.trans: We tried the recipe one more time, though we reduced the sugar slightly.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle from root س-و-ي. Means level/flat for surfaces, and 'well-cooked/ripe' for food.

examples.text: حطّه على سطح مستوي.
examples.trans: Put it on a level surface.

examples.text: الطاولة مش مستوية بتتهز.
examples.trans: The table isn't level, it wobbles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مشاكل.

examples.text: ما في أي مشكلة بحجزك.
examples.trans: There is no problem at all with your booking.

examples.text: لكل مشكلة في حل بسيط.
examples.trans: Every problem has a simple solution.

meanings.note: Form IV passive participle of أطلق; also forms the adverbial phrase على الإطلاق (at all).

examples.text: كان في هدوء مطلق بالقاعة وقت الفحص.
examples.trans: There was absolute silence in the hall during the exam.

examples.text: أعطوه حرية مطلقة باختيار مكونات الكيكة.
examples.trans: They gave him complete freedom in choosing the cake ingredients.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic bakery noun for pastries and baked doughs.

examples.text: جبنا صحن معجنات مشكلة بالجبنة والزعتر للفطور.
examples.trans: We brought a platter of assorted cheese and za'atar pastries for breakfast.

examples.text: المخبز هاد مشهور بالمعجنات الطازة كل يوم الصبح.
examples.trans: This bakery is famous for its fresh pastries every morning.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun (f. pl.) used across Jordan for roasted almonds, pistachios, walnuts, and cashews.

examples.text: رشينا مكسرات محمصة على وجه الكيكة.
examples.trans: We sprinkled roasted nuts on top of the cake.

examples.text: قدمنا الشاي مع صحن فواكه ومكسرات.
examples.trans: We served tea with a plate of fruit and nuts.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of لطّخ (to smear/stain); describes ink, paint, or jam stains.

examples.text: الحبر كان ملطخ على الزاوية التحتانية للورقة.
examples.trans: The ink was smudged on the bottom corner of the sheet.

examples.text: إيديه ملطخة بعجين وطحين من الخبيز.
examples.trans: His hands are smeared with dough and flour from baking.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.text: أنا من الأردن.
examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.text: مين رن الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.text: هذا الإبريق مصنوع من نحاس.
examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.text: هاد الولد شاطر كثير.
examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.text: لمين هدول المفاتيح النحاس؟
examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?

examples.text: صرت أحب هدول الرنتين!
examples.trans: I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Formal/educated yes-no question marker also heard in careful Jordanian speech; often omitted in casual speech.

examples.text: هل هادا هو الدفتر اللي كنت تدور عليه؟
examples.trans: Is this the notebook you were looking for?

examples.text: ما بعرف هل المكتبة فاتحة اليوم أو مسكرة.
examples.trans: I do not know whether the library is open today or closed.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.

examples.text: خلصنا كتابة الملاحظات هلق تماما.
examples.trans: We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.text: هو اللي حكى هيك.
examples.trans: He is the one who said so.

examples.text: طارق هو اللي اقترح نطلع رحلة على البترا.
examples.trans: Tareq is the one who suggested we take a trip to Petra.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: في واحد بيسأل عنك.
examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Form III verb from وزن (weight); commonly used for balancing flavours in a recipe.

examples.text: الليمون بوازن حلاوة العسل بالكيكة.
examples.trans: Lemon balances the sweetness of the honey in the cake.

examples.text: سلمى وازنت بين النكهات بدقة شاطرة.
examples.trans: Salma balanced the flavours with clever precision.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.text: أعطاني الدكتور وصفة الدواء.
examples.trans: The doctor gave me the medicine prescription.

examples.text: جربت وصفة الكعك تبعت خالتي وطلعت بتشهي.
examples.trans: I tried my aunt's cookie recipe and it turned out mouthwatering.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.text: يا أحمد، تعال هون.
examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.text: اليوم يوم طويل.
examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
